title: Wiring — Main Gear Bay Harness — Re-Routing Clear of the Gear Door Actuator Sweep

ata.title: Centre Fuselage Wiring — Landing Gear Bay Wiring

abstract: Re-routing of the main gear bay harness forty millimetres outboard and relocation of its terminal block, so that the harness is clear of the gear door actuator sweep in all door positions.

sections.planning_reason: Insulation damage in the main gear bay harness was reported thirty-eight times between 2019 and 2021, always on the same section and always on aircraft operating from stations where the bay collects debris and standing water. The harness runs within twenty millimetres of the gear door actuator sweep and the clearance is consumed whenever the harness is re-clipped after a component change. Two events produced a gear door position indication fault in flight and one led to an unscheduled gear swing on the ground.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin re-routes the harness forty millimetres outboard along the bay roof, clear of the actuator sweep in all door positions, moves the contactor with it, and relocates the terminal block to a new bracket on the bay side wall. The bus bar is re-terminated at the new position, shortening the run by a third of a metre.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft on its wheels with the gear down and locked, install the ground locks and hold the gear doors open on the ground props. Depressurise the green hydraulic system. Get access to zones 145, 572 and 721. Label and disconnect the harness at the terminal block FIN 1396VC and at the bus bar FIN 622VC7. Remove the existing clips and lay the harness clear. Mark out the side wall bracket position from the template, drill and de-burr, and apply the protection scheme to all bare material. Install the bracket and relocate the terminal block onto it. Move the contactor BED352373-29 to the new position. Re-route the harness along the revised path shown on drawing D92311222260 and secure it with the ties AGS700897-7A at the pitch given in the instructions. Re-terminate the bus bar and shorten the run to the dimension in the instructions. Measure the clearance to the actuator through a full door cycle at three positions. Do a continuity and insulation check on every circuit and a gear swing following task AMM-Z-92-31-12-200-040-A.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to aircraft in the MSN Z04196 to Z11011 range. One stored aircraft is excluded. Aircraft delivered from the production cut-in already have the revised route. The side wall bracket is drilled at embodiment, so the change cannot be reversed.
sections.material_note: Kit K9231-1002-01 contains the side wall bracket, the tie set, the harness support hardware and the drill template for one aircraft. The template is returned after use. Most of the elapsed time is re-termination and testing rather than routing.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 30 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, or at the next landing gear bay activity of two shifts or more, whichever occurs first.

ata.title: Centre Fuselage Wiring — Landing Gear Bay Wiring

abstract: Re-routing of the main gear bay harness forty millimetres outboard with its terminal block relocated, re-issued to state the cable tie section explicitly because a substituted tie pulls the harness back into the actuator sweep.

sections.planning_reason: Insulation damage in the main gear bay harness was reported thirty-eight times between 2019 and 2021, always on the same section and always on aircraft operating from stations where the bay collects debris and standing water. The harness runs within twenty millimetres of the gear door actuator sweep and the clearance is consumed whenever the harness is re-clipped after a component change. Two events produced a gear door position indication fault in flight and one led to an unscheduled gear swing on the ground.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin re-routes the harness forty millimetres outboard along the bay roof, clear of the actuator sweep in all door positions, moves the contactor with it, and relocates the terminal block to a new bracket on the bay side wall. The bus bar is re-terminated at the new position, shortening the run by a third of a metre. The cable tie is a controlled item and not a general consumable: a tie of a smaller section pulls the harness inboard as it is tightened and gives back the clearance the re-route was done to create, and several of the reporting aircraft were found with substituted ties fitted at their last bay component change.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft on its wheels with the gear down and locked, install the ground locks and hold the gear doors open on the ground props. Depressurise the green hydraulic system. Get access to zones 145, 572 and 721. Label and disconnect the harness at the terminal block FIN 1396VC and at the bus bar FIN 622VC7. Remove the existing clips and lay the harness clear. Mark out the side wall bracket position from the template, drill and de-burr, and apply the protection scheme to all bare material. Install the bracket and relocate the terminal block onto it. Move the contactor BED352373-29 to the new position. Re-route the harness along the revised path shown on drawing D92311222260 and secure it with the ties AGS700897-7A at the pitch given in the instructions. Use no other tie: the specified part is the only one whose section holds the harness on the outboard path, and a substitute of a smaller section is what puts it back under the actuator. Re-terminate the bus bar and shorten the run to the dimension in the instructions. Measure the clearance to the actuator through a full door cycle at three positions. Do a continuity and insulation check on every circuit and a gear swing following task AMM-Z-92-31-12-200-040-A.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to aircraft in the MSN Z04196 to Z11011 range. One stored aircraft is excluded. Aircraft delivered from the production cut-in already have the revised route. The side wall bracket is drilled at embodiment, so the change cannot be reversed.
sections.material_note: Kit K9231-1002-01 contains the side wall bracket, the tie set, the harness support hardware and the drill template for one aircraft. The template is returned after use. The tie set is sized for the whole bay run with a margin for later component changes; order a replacement set rather than substituting a station tie, and hold the part number AGS700897-7A on the bay work card. Most of the elapsed time is re-termination and testing rather than routing.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 30 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, or at the next landing gear bay activity of two shifts or more, whichever occurs first.
